documents.label: A
documents.citation: Huey Long, "Share Our Wealth" Radio Address, February 23, 1934 (Congressional Record, public domain)
documents.excerpt: How many men ever went to a barbecue and would let one man take off the table what was intended for nine-tenths of the people to eat? The same is true of the old U.S.A. Any man with a thimble full of sense ought to know that if you make 3 persons work to give 1 person what the 3 have earned, that the 1 person is getting 75 percent of all that is produced and that the other 3 are only getting 25 percent of what they produce...We must limit the size of the big man's fortune.

documents.label: B
documents.citation: American Liberty League Statement of Principles, 1934 (Library of Congress, public domain)
documents.excerpt: The organization of a non-partisan body...to defend and uphold the Constitution...to teach the necessity of respect for the rights of persons and property as fundamental to every form of government...The League was formed to combat what its founders believed to be an unconstitutional extension of federal power that threatened the American system of free enterprise and individual liberty.

documents.label: C
documents.citation: United States Supreme Court, Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495 (1935) (public domain)
documents.excerpt: Congress cannot delegate legislative powers to the President to such an extent as to confer unlimited authority...The attempted delegation of that authority here is clearly excessive...Extraordinary conditions do not create or enlarge constitutional power. The Constitution established a national government with powers deemed to be adequate for the governmental purposes of the founders. We look to the Constitution itself, and to its history, for the solution of constitutional questions.
